note: Why each owed code vocabulary is owed — the half [catalog §2.3]'s `x-owed` annotation and the glossary's Owed page could not say. A `data/` table is documentation and not a published constraint ([A6 §3.2(d)], [A9 §9.1]), but the `reason` here IS emitted, as the per-vocabulary `x-owed` sentence, so each one has to read on the wire without this repo. The `state` is declared here AND derived independently from `src/` — a vocabulary is refused iff it carries a live `Exact<…, OwedCode<'v'>>` gate — and a conformance test holds the two in agreement in both directions. Two declarations, not one derived from the other. THE TABLE IS PER-VOCABULARY, AND A REFUSED *MEMBER* OF AN OPEN VOCABULARY HAS NO ROW HERE — recorded 2026-10-09 because [A8 §9 item 2]'s plan told the next session to look for one. That round refused `Trusted Agent` and `Claims Manager` as members of `ROLE_NAMES`: they fail [A8 §2]'s addition test (one is an escalation contact 'readily accessible to DoW PPA', the other a DPS disclosure requirement, and neither asserts a fact). But `ROLE_NAMES` itself is not refused — [A8 §2] calls it 'provisional' and item 2 stays open — so there is no owed vocabulary whose state changed and nothing to put in a `state` field. Their refusal lives in [A8 §9 item 2]'s annotation, which is the only place a per-member decision can live. Distinguish three things before adding a row: a vocabulary refused (`identityScheme`, `roleClass` — they belong here), a member refused from an open vocabulary (item 2's two — they do not), and a FIELD refused outright ([A8 §9 item 3]'s party class — no row either, because a row here needs a live `Exact<…, OwedCode<'v'>>` gate and minting one would invent the slot the decision declines).

states.meaning: The gap closes when someone reads the sources. No argument stands in the way.

The sources ARE read and they argue against publishing a closed list. The gap does not close by effort; a round that closes it has to overturn an argument first, and the type-level gate is what stops that happening silently.
